reason: Prior measurements show large run-to-run variation and no promoted panel32 change, so they do not support causal performance claims. Test the small active-loop scheduling edits first: moving pointer updates between FMOPA operations may overlap work, while SUBS/B.NE is simple but still uses two instructions and may not reduce loop-control cost. The software pipeline has greater bounds and register-pressure risk. Prefetch is bounded but adds hints and a guard. Scratch blocking adds loop and packing complexity. The remaining proposals change layouts or transpose handling, with higher traffic, allocation, and correctness risk; the n=512 path does not use the fallback transpose, so that proposal has weak relevance to the timed workload.
